title: Newtype Pattern
summary: Wrap existing types in single-element tuple structs to enforce strict type checking.
lecture: A newtype is a wrapper around an existing primitive or structure, defined as a tuple struct with one field.
Unlike type aliases, newtypes create a completely distinct type at compile time. The compiler prevents accidental parameter swapping and wrong assignments.
At runtime, the wrapper has zero memory overhead because Rust strips the tuple struct during optimization.

example.caption: UserId wraps a u32 into a distinct type.
